question: Explain why Ohm's law is not valid for all conducting devices. Give reason using the nature of the $V-I$ relation.

options.A: Ohm's law is valid for all devices because every $V-I$ graph is linear.
options.B: Ohm's law is not valid for all devices because many have a non-linear $V-I$ relation, so current is not directly proportional to potential difference and $V/I$ is not constant.
options.C: Ohm's law is invalid only when the potential difference is zero.
options.D: Ohm's law fails for all metallic conductors because their $V-I$ relation is always non-linear.
